preamble: Palatalization of the bilabial nasal [m] to the palatal nasal [ɲ] before front vowels, with loss of the labial closure. It is characteristic of Eastern Romance: in the Moldavian dialect of Romanian the labials p, b, m become [c, ɟ, ɲ] before front vowels (miel [ɲʲel] 'lamb'), and in Aromanian the change is general, so Latin mel 'honey' and mīlia 'thousands' give njari and njilji, where nj spells [ɲ]. Bantu passive and diminutive forms with m > ɲ are morphologically conditioned alternations and are not counted here.

examples.note: The labials p, b, m become [c, ɟ, ɲ] before front vowels in the Moldavian dialect (copil [koˈkʲil] 'child', bine [ˈɡʲini] 'well').
